sections.h2: Who sends the bill and who sets the value
sections.html:
Valuation belongs to the Martin County Property Appraiser; billing and collection belong to the Martin County Tax Collector. Both are constitutional offices of the county, while recorded deeds and liens live in the clerk's Official Records.

  • Martin County Property Appraiser: real property parcel search by parcel ID, account number, subdivision, address or owner last name, plus published millage.
  • Martin County Tax Collector: tax statements, alternative payment plans, delinquent taxes and certificates, an important-dates page, a tangible personal property page and a glossary. Offices operate in Stuart, Hobe Sound, Indiantown and Palm City, and the phone line is 772-288-5600.
  • Martin County Clerk Official Records: the search for recorded instruments.

Amounts owed go to the collector. Value, exemptions and parcel records go to the appraiser. Ten taxing authorities levy tax on Martin County parcels, and each proposes its own millage rate before public hearings set the budgets.

sections.h2: Where to pay and get help
sections.html:
The tax collector runs four offices: Stuart, Hobe Sound, Indiantown and Palm City. Its home page posts estimated wait times for each office, and e-checks cost nothing. An account can be looked up through the online payment pages or the county-taxes portal with no trip needed.

The site also carries a glossary of tax terms, a page on tangible personal property taxes, an FAQ on tax certificate sales and a page on alternative payment plans. Site information can change daily and is not a legal guarantee, the collector warns, so phone to confirm any amount before you rely on it at a closing.

To understand the value side, use the appraiser's parcel search and compare your TRIM notice with the published roll data. Lenders and title companies commonly request the appraiser record along with the collector's account history.

sections.h2: When Martin County property taxes are due
sections.html:
Mailing usually happens around November 1, and the gross amount must be paid by March 31. The early discount starts at 4% in November and ends at 1% in February.

Martin County tax calendar
MonthEvent and deadline
NovemberCollection begins, 4% discount through November 30
December3% discount; third installment due by December 31 with 3% discount
January2% discount
February1% discount
MarchGross amount due by March 31; fourth installment due
AprilUnpaid real property taxes delinquent on April 1; applications for the next installment year due by April 30
JuneCertificate sale starts by June 1; first installment due by June 30 with 6% discount
SeptemberSecond installment due by September 30 with 4.5% discount

Starting April 1, unpaid real property taxes carry 3% interest. Unpaid business personal property accrues 1.5% per month plus a $2.00 delinquent fee, and those accounts are advertised in a local newspaper within 45 days.

On real estate, an ad appears in the newspaper each week for three weeks ahead of the certificate sale, and the parcel is charged for it. Whoever buys the certificate must hold off two years before asking the owner for payment; a tax deed application may follow.

sections.h2: Business and vehicle taxes on the collector's calendar
sections.html:
The calendar covers more than real estate. Business personal property earns the same early discounts and turns delinquent on the same April 1. Warrants for delinquent personal property accounts are prepared before April 30, two years after the assessment year.

  • Local business tax receipts: renewals are due September 30 and become delinquent October 1, when a late fee applies.
  • Heavy trucks over 5,000 pounds, truck-trailers, semi-trailers and certain vehicles for hire: registration and renewal due December 31.
  • Mobile home decals: they also expire December 31.

Rental owners and anyone running a business from the property should ask the collector about these items, since a house sale does not shut down a business account attached to the address.

sections.h2: Is there an installment plan in Martin County?
sections.html:
Yes, section 197.222 allows an alternative payment plan of four payments. Applications for the next year close April 30.

  • June 30: first payment with a 6% discount.
  • July: a late first payment may be accepted with a 5% penalty, otherwise participation is canceled.
  • September 30: second payment with a 4.5% discount.
  • December 31: third payment with a 3% discount.
  • March 31: fourth and final payment.

Once enrolled, taxpayers continue without reapplying. Selling midway through the plan means asking the collector for the unpaid portion, which is settled at closing.

sections.h2: Exemptions that can lower a Martin County bill
sections.html:
Filing is with the property appraiser, and the first deadline is early March.

  • Homestead takes up to $50,000 off value. School taxes see only the first $25,000 of it.
  • A state cap limits yearly growth on a homestead. The state chart prints 2.7% for 2026.
  • Other property has a 10 percent annual ceiling.
  • Portability carries cap savings to a new homestead, for up to $500,000 of difference. Chapter 2026-239 changes first apply to the 2027 roll.
  • An honorably discharged Florida resident with a service-connected disability of 10 percent or more receives a $5,000 cut in assessed value.

A sale resets the parcel to market-based value the following January. The TRIM notice arrives in August, and petitions go to the clerk.

sections.h2: How Martin County tax is settled at a sale
sections.html:
The collector's payoff number lets the title company clear the tax when the sale funds. All four offices, in Stuart, Hobe Sound, Indiantown and Palm City, can be reached at 772-288-5600 about whether a certificate exists.

Florida charges deed stamp tax at 70 cents per $100 of consideration. A contract-for-deed buyer on record is among those notified before a tax deed sale, so a land contract does not hide a parcel from the process.

  1. Get the payoff figure and certificate details from the collector.
  2. Give the closing agent a record of any installments paid.
  3. Check the settlement statement's tax line before you sign.

A cash sale skips lender underwriting, but title work still looks for unpaid tax, so the same steps apply.

sections.h2: Preparing to sell with a Martin County tax account
sections.html:
A short routine before listing keeps tax questions from slowing a contract.

  1. Look up the parcel with the appraiser and confirm the owner name and mailing address.
  2. Ask the collector for the account history and any certificate or delinquent balance.
  3. If you are enrolled in the installment plan, list the payments made so far.
  4. If a business or rental account is tied to the property, close or transfer it with the collector.
  5. Keep your latest TRIM notice and tax statement on hand for buyers and lenders.

Because amounts change daily, confirm the payoff again a few days before closing and send the final figure to the closing agent. The buyer should also expect a higher bill after the sale, since value resets to market.

faqs.q: When are Martin County property tax statements mailed?
faqs.a: On or about November 1 each year. The gross amount is due by March 31.

faqs.q: What interest does Martin County add after April 1?
faqs.a: A 3% interest charge on unpaid real property taxes. Tangible personal property accrues 1.5% per month plus a $2.00 fee.

faqs.q: Does Martin County have an installment plan for property tax?
faqs.a: Yes. Four payments fall on June 30, September 30, December 31 and March 31, with discounts of 6%, 4.5% and 3% on the first three. Applications are due by April 30.

faqs.q: Who do I call in Martin County about my tax account?
faqs.a: Call the Martin County Tax Collector at 772-288-5600. For parcel values and exemptions, contact the Martin County Property Appraiser.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Martin County house if taxes are overdue?
faqs.a: Yes. The balance can be cleared at closing. Get the payoff and any certificate details from the collector beforehand.
